target_customer: Mobile app and web developers who want to grow through user invites
problem: Apps struggle to turn contact imports and invite flows into growth because users do not know whom to invite.
business_model: Usage-based developer API priced by attributable growth, planned
product_category: Referral and invite recommendation API, growth tooling

founders.name: Ivan Kirigin
founders.background_notes: The YC page also lists Lyft, which followed the 2017 acquisition. TechCrunch 2015 calls him a former head of growth at Dropbox.

exit.reason: Lyft acquired YesGraph with another user acquisition startup; the public API was shut down afterward. Price undisclosed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Ranking contacts by invite acceptance probability needed machine learning and social graph data plus enrichment, with a small team and limited early data.

defensibility.rationale: Value depended on data accumulated across customer apps, but large social networks already ran growth teams with their own data and the product was a feature for many apps.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large networks kept the capability in house. Lyft bought the team in August 2017 and the public API was turned off.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in February 2015 said larger social networks already had big growth and referral teams, implying smaller apps needed the capability, and pilot customers were lined up.

branding.domain_note: Used yesgraph.com; acquisition of the domain was not found.

identity.logo: Not described in the sources found
identity.visual_style: Developer tool styling, not documented in the sources found
identity.voice_and_tone: Technical, likened its product to People You May Know on LinkedIn

brand_strength.rationale: No source shows press about the brand itself, community or a recognisable identity beyond developer docs.

pivots.from: Referral engine for recruiting and hiring candidates (covered Jan 2014)
pivots.to: Invite recommendation API for mobile apps
pivots.why: TechCrunch says the company originally built a recruiting tool on the same engine

outcome_analysis: YesGraph raised $1.3M for a recruiting referral product and then $1M in February 2015 to sell invite recommendations to app developers, led by Bloomberg Beta. The product was still in private beta with no pricing at that point. Lyft acquired the company in August 2017 and shut the public API, which matches a small team absorbed for its growth expertise rather than a standalone product outcome.
